sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier dimorphic, major and minor. Major: head dark orange-red, the posterior half of the head hemispherical and hairless, the anterior part slightly constricted, the nasus long and slender, slightly more than 2/3 of the total head length; antennae 13-segmented; mandibles without pointed teeth. Minor: generally similar to the major but distinctly smaller, the head much narrower and slightly more constricted, widest in the posterior 1/3, narrowing distinctly from there to the base of the nasus, antennae 12-segmented. The major soldier differs from E. tumuli in the more slender base of the nasus, the different proportions of the antennal segments, and the much paler colour of head, thorax, abdomen and legs; the minor soldier is likewise paler and has a more constricted head. Worker head dark reddish brown, antennae 14-segmented, segment 4 the shortest and narrowest of all. The alate is not recorded in the original.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text:
Major: head dark orange-red, the apex of the nasus usually dark rusty; antennae, thorax and abdominal sternites pale brown, the antennae darkest, the femora and abdominal tergites paler than the sternites, the tibiae white. Posterior half of the head hemispherical and hairless, the anterior part slightly constricted; nasus long and slender, slightly more than 2/3 of the total head length, the apex with many short hairs; in profile the dorsum nearly straight, with a shallow concavity slightly behind the middle. Antennae 13-segmented; segment 2 about half of segment 1 and 1/3 narrower, nearly cylindrical; segment 3 shorter than or equal to segment 2, narrow at the base; segment 4 the shortest and narrowest of all; segment 5 about as long as segment 2 but wider; segments 6—12 slightly longer than segment 5; segment 13 as long as segment 2. Thorax and abdomen with very few hairs. Mandibles without pointed teeth. Minor: generally similar to the major but distinctly smaller, the head much narrower and slightly more constricted. Sides of the head narrowing distinctly from the widest point (posterior 1/3) to the base of the nasus. Antennae 12-segmented; segment 3 always the smallest of all; segment 4 longer and wider than segment 2; segment 5 shorter than segments 4 and 6; otherwise as in the major. Mandibles without pointed teeth.
Measurements: major body length 3.25—3.60 mm, head length (to apex of nasus) 1.50—1.60 mm, head width 0.73—0.80 mm, pronotum width 0.40—0.45 mm; minor body length 2.50—2.75 mm, head length (to apex of nasus) 1.18—1.33 mm, head width 0.55—0.59 mm, pronotum width 0.33—0.36 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text:
Head dark reddish brown, darker than in the soldier, the transverse and median sutures very distinct (white); the transverse suture expands anterolaterally into a large straw-yellow area and extends posteriorly on the sides of the head as two more or less distinct broad lines; postclypeus orange-yellow, sometimes tinged pale brown; labrum pale straw-yellow; thoracic and abdominal tergites tinged brown. Head longer than wide, widest anteriorly, narrowing to the broadly rounded posterior margin, with very few short hairs. Postclypeus strongly convex, more than half as long as wide. Antennae 14-segmented; segment 4 the shortest and narrowest of all.
Measurements: body length 4.00 mm; head length (to apex of labrum) 1.43—1.55 mm; head length (to clypeofrontal suture) 0.80—0.92 mm; head width 1.10—1.14 mm; pronotum width 0.55—0.60 mm.

note: Adapted from the species-level description in Hill (1942), originally in English; the original reads Eutermes petilus sp. nov. (the heading line OCR'd as "Futernes pGtilus"), type locality Tammin (the original OCR "Tainmin"), also recorded from Merredin, Northam, Toodyay, Mullewa. The alate is recorded in the original as "Not known", so no section is given for it. In Affinities the sentence describing the antennal differences of the major soldier is severely garbled in the OCR ("the antennae have w?ZV e f n i a i °n") and has not been translated; the lead should check it against the original book.
